newsitem.title: USA: Citizens sells servicing rights for $89 mln. [CORRECTED 14:27 GMT 23/12]
newsitem.headline: Citizens sells servicing rights for $89 mln. [CORRECTED 14:27 GMT 23/12]

text.p: Citizens Financial Group, 76.5 percent-owned by the Royal Bank of Scotland Group Plc, said on Wednesday it completed the sale of $5 billion (corrects from $45 billion) worth of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac mortgage servicing rights for about $89 million.
The company said it sold the rights to Dovenmuehle who will also subservice $3.2 billion of bank-owned mortgages for Citizens and $3.8 billion of investor mortgage servicing rights.
The deal was approved by the Federal Trade Commission to be transferred in the first quarter of 1997, the company said.
Freddie Mac is the commonly used name for the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. Fannie Mae is short for the Federal National Mortgage Association.

The company said it continues to explore strategic options for the investor mortgage servicing rights portfolio. It also said the Royal Bank of Ireland owns the portion of Citizens not owned by the Royal Bank of Scotland.
